rows.jp: 新川豊は元気だった。いつもだいたい。
rows.en: Yutaka Shinkawa was lively. Most of the time.

ghs.en: Shinkawa Yutaka was in high spirits. Almost always.

rows.jp: レスポンスが早い。

ghs.en: Replies came quick.

rows.jp: 話していてキレが良かった。
rows.en: Talking with him had a nice snap to it.

ghs.en: The way he talked was sharp and clever.

rows.jp: ノリも良かった。
rows.en: He knew how to play along, too.

ghs.en: Quite good on the back-and-forth of jokes, too.

rows.jp: その新川が、ある時こんなことを言った。
rows.en: Then one day, Shinkawa said this.

ghs.en: Shinkawa once said this:

rows.jp: 『姪がさー、やっぱ群青行くんだけどさ、いろいろ教えてやらんと』
rows.en: ‘My niece is going to Gunjo after all, so I’ve gotta teach her the ropes.’

ghs.en: Shinkawa: 『Got a niece, ya know, 'course she goes to Gunjou, ya know, so she's telling me lots and lots of stuff.』
ghs.assessment: Shinkawa says his niece will also attend Gunjō and that he needs to teach her various things. The English says she already attends and reverses the teaching direction so that she tells him things.

highlights.text: Shinkawa: 『Got a niece, ya know, 'course she goes to Gunjou, ya know, so she's telling me lots and lots of stuff.』

rows.jp: 揉めた。

ghs.en: We discussed it harshly.

rows.jp: しかも相当に可愛いとのこと。
rows.en: Apparently, she was also extremely cute.

ghs.en: How she was fairly cute, for starters.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese adds that she is reportedly quite cute. The English is an ungoverned 'how' fragment and makes the statement the first item in an unstated list.

highlights.text: How she was fairly cute, for starters.

rows.jp: さらに揉めた。羨望と嫉妬だった。
rows.en: We fought some more. Envy and jealousy.

ghs.en: And we furthermore discussed. It was envy with jealousy.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the dispute or agitation intensified because of envy and jealousy. The English reduces it to further discussion and joins the two emotions with the wrong preposition.

highlights.text: we furthermore discussed. It was envy with jealousy.

rows.jp: この二つが揃えば、だいたいどんな相手でも憎める。人間は。
rows.en: Give a person both, and they can hate almost anyone. Such is humanity.

ghs.en: If both of those are present, hatred would normally ensue, and regardless of who's their target. It's human.

rows.jp: 俺は憎みはしなかった。

ghs.en: I did not have hatred.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Taichi did not hate him. The English nominalizes the feeling and omits its object.

highlights.text: I did not have hatred.

rows.jp: 続く豊の発言が、よりさらなる衝撃を引き起こしたからだ。
rows.en: Because what Yutaka said next delivered an even greater shock.

ghs.en: But the next remark by Yutaka provoked even further jolts in me:

rows.jp: 『本気で、妹みたいなもんなんだよ。同居してるし』
rows.en: ‘Seriously, she’s like a little sister to me. We live together and everything.’

ghs.en: Shinkawa: 『Seriously, she's kinda like a little sister, 's all. 's just cohabitation.』
ghs.assessment: Shinkawa says the niece is like a little sister because they live together. The English adds a separate fragment dismissing the situation as 'just cohabitation.'

highlights.text: 's just cohabitation

rows.jp: 可愛い血の繋がらない妹的存在と暮らしている。
rows.en: He lived with a cute, unrelated, little-sister-like presence.

ghs.en: He is living together with a Cute Non-Blood Related Imouto-like being.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes living with a cute, unrelated, little-sister-like figure. The English leaves imouto untranslated, capitalizes the entire description, and dehumanizes her as a 'being.'

highlights.text: Cute Non-Blood Related Imouto-like being

rows.jp: しかも後に聞いたところでは、両親はほとんど家に帰らないらしい。
rows.en: And as I later learned, her parents were almost never home.

ghs.en: And also, some time later I heard that their parents seemed to almost never be home.

rows.jp: こういうシチュを、逸般的に同棲と言います。
rows.en: In aberrant parlance, this situation is known as cohabitation.

ghs.en: The abovementioned 'chewation is ungenerally referred to as 'sharing the house'.

rows.jp: 二人とも群青に通うことになる。
rows.en: Now they would both be attending Gunjo.

ghs.en: The two of them ended up both going to Gunjou.
ghs.assessment: The place name 群青 is Gunjō in standard Hepburn, not 'Gunjou.'

highlights.text: Gunjou

rows.jp: 『おー、姪のことも紹介してやるよ』
rows.en: ‘Sure, I’ll introduce you to my niece.’

ghs.en: Shinkawa: 『Oh, I'll be introducing you to the niece then!』

rows.jp: 『……たいしたもんじゃないんだけどな……あんま期待すんなよ？』
rows.en: ‘...She’s nothing special, though... Don’t get your hopes up, okay?’

ghs.en: Shinkawa: 『...it ain't much of a big deal so... don't expect much, will ya?』
ghs.assessment: Shinkawa says that his niece is nothing special. The English substitutes an impersonal 'it' and describes a situation as no big deal.

highlights.text: it ain't much of a big deal

rows.jp: たいしたものじゃない。

ghs.en: Not much of a big deal.
ghs.assessment: The narration repeats that she is supposedly nothing special. The English again turns the person into an unspecified situation.

highlights.text: Not much of a big deal.

rows.jp: 後に俺は、実際に彼女と会うことになった。
rows.en: Later, I actually did meet her.

ghs.en: Later on, I ended up meeting her for real.

rows.jp: 「じゃ紹介すると、こいつが佐倉霧。家族みたいなモン」
rows.en: “Introductions, then. This is Kiri Sakura. She’s like family.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Introductions then, this here's Sakura Kiri. She's sorta like family."

rows.jp: 一般的にこれを青天の霹靂と言います。
rows.en: In ordinary parlance, this is known as a bolt from the blue.

ghs.en: The abovementioned is generally referred to as a 'thunderbolt out of the blue'.

rows.jp: 「どうした、二人とも黙っちゃって？　もしかして二人とも、照れちゃってるのか？　おいおい霧はともかく太一、こんな山猿に照れる必要ねーって」
rows.en: “What’s with you two going quiet? Are you both embarrassed? Come on, Kiri I can understand, but Taichi, there’s no need to get shy over some mountain monkey.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "What's it, you guys just shut up? Don'tcha tell me, you guys're all shy? C'mon, c'mon, I understand Kiri, but Taichi, no need to be all shy in front of this bumpkin, right!"
ghs.assessment: Shinkawa says that Kiri may be shy, but Taichi need not be shy around this mountain bumpkin. The English's 'I understand Kiri' changes the concession into comprehension and leaves the bumpkin's referent unclear.

highlights.text: Shinkawa: "What's it, you guys just shut up? Don'tcha tell me, you guys're all shy? C'mon, c'mon, I understand Kiri, but Taichi, no need to be all shy in front of this bumpkin, right!"

rows.jp: 「豊、うるさい……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Yutaka, shut up..."

rows.jp: 「……佐倉霧、です」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...I am Sakura Kiri."

rows.jp: 「く、黒須太一です」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I-, I am Kurosu Taichi."

rows.jp: ぎこちなく頭を下げる。

ghs.en: I bow my head in awkward embarrassment.

rows.jp: 「お、お噂はかねがね」

ghs.en: Taichi: "He-, heard quite a lot about you."
Kiri: "...huh."

rows.jp: あの戦慄の踵(かかと)使い……だったのだ。
rows.en: She was the mistress of that terrifying heel.

ghs.en: It was her... that terrifying heel user.

rows.jp: 確か復讐を誓って別れた。
rows.en: If I recalled correctly, we had parted after swearing revenge.

ghs.en: We certainly parted with vows of revenge.

rows.jp: 霧の目に、好意のかけらさえ、まったく見受けられない。
rows.en: There was not the slightest speck of goodwill in Kiri’s eyes.

ghs.en: I could not catch a glint of favoritism in Kiri's eyes.
ghs.assessment: 好意 means goodwill, affection, or favor toward Taichi. 'Favoritism' means unfair preferential treatment and changes the interpersonal judgment.

highlights.text: favoritism

rows.jp: というか、ジト目である。
rows.en: If anything, she was glaring daggers at me.

ghs.en: Or should I say, she's staring at me scornfully.

rows.jp: 「こちらもいろいろと噂、聞いてます」
rows.en: “I’ve heard all sorts of stories about you, too.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "I have also heard a lot about you, heard indeed."

rows.jp: 「そ、そう？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ha-, have you?"

rows.jp: 俺は緊張しつつ、ティーカップを口につけた。
rows.en: Tense, I raised the teacup to my lips.

ghs.en: I put the teacup to my mouth despite the mental strain.

rows.jp: 「いやー、この紅茶、甘いなー！　まるで砂糖みたい、うん。それになんだかざらざらするね。新食感ってやつか」
rows.en: “Wow, this tea is sweet! Just like sugar, yeah. And somehow it’s gritty, too. Is this one of those exciting new textures?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wooow, this black tea's sweet ain't iiit! It's just like sugar, yes. And somehow just a little coarse and granular. It's a novel food texture ain't it."

rows.jp: きつい。

ghs.en: Harsh.

rows.jp: ことほどさようにツッコミとは、ある意味慈愛でもあるのだ。
rows.en: A corrective retort, in this sense, is also an act of mercy.

ghs.en: The performance of a Straight-Man Retort is, in a certain sense, a representation of reciprocal kindness.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that tsukkomi is in one sense an act of benevolence. The English invents capitalization and 'reciprocal,' while its cumbersome gloss describes a performed representation rather than the retort itself.

highlights.text: a Straight-Man Retort is, in a certain sense, a representation of reciprocal kindness

rows.jp: 「つうか、ナチュラルに砂糖じゃん、それ」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Right, naturally, ain't it sugar that."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says, 'That's literally just sugar.' The English forms neither a grammatical question nor declaration.

highlights.text: ain't it sugar that

rows.jp: 「……いたみいる」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...I am greatly obliged."

rows.jp: 身に染みた。

ghs.en: It's something that went all the way down to the heart.
ghs.assessment: 身に染みた means that the remark hit home or sank in. The English literalizes a physical path and uses 'to' rather than an idiomatic emotional construction.

highlights.text: went all the way down to the heart

rows.jp: 「……なんでも、手当たり次第にセクハラをしてらっしゃるとか」
rows.en: “...I understand that you sexually harass anyone and everyone you come across.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...I am told that you perform sexual harassment on anyone and everyone you can lay your hands on."

rows.jp: 「そーなんだよコイツ、やることすげーの。かなりびびるよ」
rows.en: “Yeah, this guy is unbelievable. The stuff he does will seriously freak you out.”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Doooes 'e now, this guy, that's some weeeird stuff he does. Pretty freaky!"
ghs.assessment: Shinkawa agrees that this is what Taichi does and says his behavior is extreme. The English turns the opening into a malformed question and leaves two competing subjects in one clause.

highlights.text: Doooes 'e now, this guy, that's some weeeird stuff he does.

rows.jp: 「ああ、いや、それはね、セクハラといいますか……その……性的愛情表現って感じで決してやましい意図ではないという」
rows.en: “Oh, no, that’s not so much sexual harassment as... well... a sexual expression of affection entirely free of improper intent.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, no, that would be well, calling it something like sexual harassment... it is... a sexual related expression of endearment that has no guilty intent whatsoever!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese calls it a sexual expression of affection. The English uses the noun 'sexual' where the compound requires 'sexually related' or a direct adjective.

highlights.text: a sexual related expression of endearment

rows.jp: 「そういうの、セクハラって言います」

ghs.en: Kiri: "And that is called, 'sexual harassment'."

rows.jp: 「あー、そうだったけかな！　ハハハ……」
rows.en: “Oh, right! Of course it does! Hahaha...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, that is what it seemed like! HA. HA. HA..."
ghs.assessment: そうだったっけ asks whether that was what the behavior was called. The English instead says the classification merely seemed that way.

highlights.text: that is what it seemed like

rows.jp: 見えないナイフが、ざくざく突き刺さってくる。
rows.en: Invisible knives stabbed into me, one after another.

ghs.en: A knife I could not see pierced me with slashes and thrusts.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese imagines multiple invisible knives stabbing into him again and again. The English reduces them to one knife and adds slashing as a separate action.

highlights.text: A knife I could not see pierced me with slashes and thrusts.

rows.jp: 「……嫌がってる子も、いますよね？」
rows.en: “...Some of the girls hate it, don’t they?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...but you do it to the reluctant ones as well, do you?"

rows.jp: 「あー、嫌がる相手にはちゃんと慎んでるよ？　その、心の底から嫌がる相手は、わかるんで、ハイ」
rows.en: “Oh, I show proper restraint with anyone who hates it. I can tell when someone hates it from the bottom of her heart. Yes.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, I'm properly prudent with reluctant partners you know? That is, I can tell when a partner is disagreeing from the bottom of the heart, yesss!"
ghs.assessment: Taichi says he properly refrains with anyone who truly dislikes it. The English substitutes being 'prudent,' calls the girls partners, and weakens deep aversion to merely disagreeing.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, I'm properly prudent with reluctant partners you know? That is, I can tell when a partner is disagreeing from the bottom of the heart, yesss!"

rows.jp: 「じゃあ、みゆきはセクハラを望んでいるんですか？」
rows.en: “Then Miyuki wants you to sexually harass her?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Did Miyuki wish to be sexually harassed then?"

rows.jp: 「あー、まあ嫌がってる、かな？　けどそれは表面的でしてな、お嬢さん。ホレ、口ではなんといっても体は正直みたいな」
rows.en: “Oh, well, she hates it, I guess? But only on the surface, young lady. You know what they say: her lips protest, but her body tells the truth.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, was she reluctant, maybe I wonder? But that's just on the surface it is, ojou-san. Yes, because even if her mouth doesn't say it, her body has evidence."
ghs.assessment: Taichi claims her reluctance is only superficial and invokes the cliche that whatever the mouth says, the body is honest. The English shifts to past tense and changes bodily honesty into unspecified 'evidence.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, was she reluctant, maybe I wonder? But that's just on the surface it is, ojou-san. Yes, because even if her mouth doesn't say it, her body has evidence."

ghs.en: Kiri: "...disgusting."

rows.jp: 吐き捨てるような小声。
rows.en: A mutter spat under her breath.

ghs.en: In a low voice, as if spitting my way.
ghs.assessment: Kiri speaks in a low voice as though spitting the words out. The English makes the narrator the object of spitting and uses 'way' without a meaningful role.

highlights.text: as if spitting my way

rows.jp: 俺には聞こえた。

ghs.en: I heard it, but,

rows.jp: バームクーヘンの縞模様を薄くはがすことに熱中している豊には、聞こえない。
rows.en: Yutaka, absorbed in peeling one thin stripe at a time from the Baumkuchen, did not.

ghs.en: Yutaka did not hear, lost as he is his enthusiastic tearing apart a Baumkuchen by thin stripes.
ghs.assessment: Yutaka is absorbed in peeling apart the cake's thin striped layers. The English omits 'in' after 'lost,' makes enthusiasm possess the action, and changes layers into a method 'by stripes.'

highlights.text: lost as he is his enthusiastic tearing apart a Baumkuchen by thin stripes

rows.jp: このガキ、空気を読むということをしないのか。
rows.en: Could this brat not read the room?

ghs.en: Can't this ghoul of a brat just not read the mood?
ghs.assessment: Taichi asks whether the brat cannot read the room. The English adds 'ghoul' and its double negative instead asks whether he can refrain from reading it.

highlights.text: Can't this ghoul of a brat just not read the mood?

rows.jp: アイサインをばちばち送る。
rows.en: I bombarded him with frantic looks.

ghs.en: Crackle, crackle an electric eye-sign is sent.
Shinkawa: "!"

rows.jp: 豊が気づく。

ghs.en: Yutaka notices.

rows.jp: そうだよ、助けてくれ！

ghs.en: Yes, help me please!

rows.jp: 俺は目で雄弁に語った。

ghs.en: I speak with eloquence via eyes.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Taichi speaks eloquently with his eyes. English requires a determiner or possessive before the plural body part.

highlights.text: via eyes

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "!!!"

rows.jp: 豊は部長クラスの誇らしげな顔で、任せておけとばかりに小さく頷く。
rows.en: Wearing the proud face of a department manager, Yutaka gave a tiny nod that said, Leave it to me.

ghs.en: With a face that's Club President Class as far as pride, Yutaka signaled a "leave it all to me!" with a tiny nod.

rows.jp: 「あ……やべ、生理はじまった。俺、ナプキン買ってくるから、その間二人で話しててくれよな？」
rows.en: “Oh... crap, my period just started. I’m gonna go buy some pads, so you two talk while I’m gone, okay?”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Ah... no way, my period's begun. I gotta put on a pad, so in the while you two get chatting will you?"
ghs.assessment: Shinkawa's excuse says he will go buy pads and asks them to talk in the meantime. The English changes buying to wearing one and uses the malformed temporal phrase 'in the while.'

highlights.text: I gotta put on a pad, so in the while

rows.jp: 霧「いて」%N太一「いてくれ、頼む」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "?"

rows.jp: 何も理解していなかった。

ghs.en: He didn't understand anything at all.

rows.jp: 二人きりになったら、気まずさの爆弾が炸裂しそうだ。
rows.en: If we were left alone, the awkwardness bomb was going to blow.

ghs.en: This bomb of unpleasantness might just explode if it's just the two of us alone.

rows.jp: 「わたしには、みゆきがスカートをめくられたがってる……とは思えないです」
rows.en: “I don’t believe Miyuki wants her skirt flipped up.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Miyuki wanted her skirt flipped you say... that did not appear to be the case to me."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says she cannot believe Miyuki wants the treatment. The English changes the present desire under discussion into a completed past desire.

highlights.text: Miyuki wanted her skirt flipped

rows.jp: 「んー、そ、そう？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Mmmh, re-, really?"

rows.jp: 豊は再び、バームクーヘンを解体しはじめる。
rows.en: Yutaka went back to dismantling the Baumkuchen.

ghs.en: Yutaka begins once more his disassembly of the Baumkuchen.

rows.jp: アカン……この人……。

ghs.en: Hopeless... this guy is just...

rows.jp: 「だから黒須先輩のしてることは、どうかと思います」
rows.en: “So I have serious doubts about what you’re doing, Kurosu.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Therefore, what you have done, Kurosu-senpai, is something I have a problem with."

rows.jp: ハッキリ言う。

ghs.en: So she says sharply.

rows.jp: 冷静に見ると、嫌いなタイプじゃない。
rows.en: Viewed calmly, she was not the kind of person I disliked.

ghs.en: Looked at calmly, she is not the disliking type.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that, viewed calmly, Kiri is not a type Taichi dislikes. The English instead says that Kiri herself is not prone to disliking others.

highlights.text: she is not the disliking type

rows.jp: むしろ好ましい……近づきたいと思わせる少女だった。
rows.en: If anything, she was a likable girl... one who made me want to get closer.

ghs.en: Rather, the likeable one... a girl that leaves me the sense of a desire to approach.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says she is actually likable, a girl who makes him want to get closer. The English lacks the subject for 'the likeable one' and converts desire into a sense she leaves him.

highlights.text: the likeable one... a girl that leaves me the sense of a desire to approach

rows.jp: 少し気が抜けた。
rows.en: Some of the tension left me.

ghs.en: I felt a bit relaxed.

rows.jp: ちゃんと話したくなった。
rows.en: I wanted to speak honestly with her.

ghs.en: I wanted to talk frankly to her.

rows.jp: 「……佐倉さんは、正義漢だな」
rows.en: “...You’ve got a strong sense of justice, Sakura.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...Sakura-san, you're a woman among women, a Woman of Justice."
ghs.assessment: 正義漢 calls her a person with a strong sense of justice. The English invents a gendered superlative and a capitalized title.

highlights.text: a woman among women, a Woman of Justice

rows.jp: むっとしたようだった。

ghs.en: She seemed to grow testy.

rows.jp: 「それがなにか？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "What would that even be?"
ghs.assessment: それがなにか means 'And what of it?' The English instead asks him to identify what the quality is.

highlights.text: What would that even be?

rows.jp: 「いや、いいんだ。そういう人間は、どこにだって必要だと思うし」
rows.en: “No, it’s a good thing. The world needs people like that everywhere.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Welll, it's a good thing. I think that's the kind of human that's necessary anywhere and everywhere."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says people like that are needed everywhere. The English uses a categorical 'kind of human' and redundantly stacks two universal location phrases.

highlights.text: the kind of human that's necessary anywhere and everywhere

rows.jp: 「……おっしゃる意味がわかりません」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...I do not understand the meaning of your words."

rows.jp: 「馬鹿にしてるんじゃないよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm not ridiculing you here!"

rows.jp: 「今まで、キミみたいなタイプ、俺のそばにいなかったからさ」
rows.en: “I’ve never had your type around me before.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Just, up until now, there's never been your kind of type around me."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says he has never had her type around him. 'Kind of type' redundantly combines two classifiers.

highlights.text: your kind of type

rows.jp: 「……そうですか」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...so you say."

rows.jp: 見たら豊は座ったまま寝ていた。
rows.en: I looked over. Yutaka had fallen asleep sitting up.

ghs.en: Looking over, Yutaka had fallen asleep while still sitting.

rows.jp: さすがマイフレン。大物である。
rows.en: That’s my friend for you. A man of immense stature.

ghs.en: Just what I expected, my friend. A VIP you are.
ghs.assessment: 大物 calls Yutaka a formidable, unflappable character. 'VIP' instead assigns social importance, and the inversion adds an unsupported voice.

highlights.text: A VIP you are.

rows.jp: おかげで少しつっこんだ話ができそうだ。
rows.en: Thanks to him, it seemed we could talk a little more deeply.

ghs.en: And because of that, it seems we can now talk a little more in depth.

rows.jp: 「群青はどう？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "How's Gunjou?"
ghs.assessment: The standard Hepburn romanization of 群青 is Gunjō, not 'Gunjou.'

highlights.text: Gunjou

rows.jp: 「……どうといいますと？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...'how' in what sense?"

rows.jp: 「クラスに編入されてさ、いろんなタイプのヤツがいる。言葉の通じないヤツ、周囲が目に入らないヤツ、突発的に暴れるヤツ、まったく普通人みたいなヤツ」
rows.en: “You transfer into a class and meet all kinds. People you can’t communicate with, people oblivious to what’s around them, people who suddenly turn violent, people who look completely ordinary.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There's all sorts of types that get put into classes. The type who can't understand your language, the type who doesn't see what's around them, the type that fires into rage suddenly, and the damnably normal-ish types."
ghs.assessment: The list describes people one cannot communicate with, people oblivious to their surroundings, people with sudden violent outbursts, and apparently ordinary people. The English narrows communication to 'your language,' literalizes perception, and adds 'damnably.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "There's all sorts of types that get put into classes. The type who can't understand your language, the type who doesn't see what's around them, the type that fires into rage suddenly, and the damnably normal-ish types."

rows.jp: 「けどみんな、世間に適応できなくて弾かれたのばっかりだ」
rows.en: “But every one of them failed to fit into society and got cast out.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But all, to the last, have been repelled by society for being unable to conform to it."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says they were rejected or excluded because they could not adapt to society. 'Repelled' depicts a physical force or mutual disgust rather than social exclusion.

highlights.text: repelled by society

rows.jp: 「みんな、日本で屈指のどうかしてる人間なんだ。もちろん、俺もキミもだよ」
rows.en: “They’re some of the most profoundly unwell people in Japan. And that includes me and you, of course.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Everybody there's one of Japan's foremost damaged humans. Of course, me and you too."
ghs.assessment: Taichi calls everyone there one of Japan's most seriously messed-up people, himself and Kiri included. The English lacks a verb, dehumanizes them as 'damaged humans,' and uses object pronouns as subjects.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Everybody there's one of Japan's foremost damaged humans. Of course, me and you too."

ghs.en: Kiri: "..."

rows.jp: 「会話できる人間が何人いる？　友達と呼べる関係を築ける相手が何人いた？」
rows.en: “How many people can you talk to? How many have you found with whom you can build something you’d call a friendship?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "How many humans there that can manage a conversation? How many that can be party to building something that can be called friendship?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks how many people can hold a conversation and with how many one can build a relationship called friendship. The first English question lacks 'are,' and the second turns a potential friend into a party to constructing an abstract thing.

highlights.text: Taichi: "How many humans there that can manage a conversation? How many that can be party to building something that can be called friendship?"

rows.jp: 「仮に会話が成立しても、そいつがどんなはずみで暴走するかわからない。不安はいつもつきまとう」
rows.en: “Even if conversation is possible, you never know what might set them off. The anxiety never leaves.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Even if we were to say that a conversation was established, you couldn't even begin to guess what spur would make them explode. Anxiety is always on your heels."

rows.jp: 「たとえば……ガラスの割れる音を聞くと、異常に攻撃的になるヤツとかさ。うちのクラスにいるんだけど」
rows.en: “For instance... there’s someone in my class who becomes violently aggressive at the sound of breaking glass.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "For example... someone who, when he hears the sound of glass being shattered, starts being abnormally aggressive. He's right in my class, you know."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the person becomes abnormally aggressive. 'Starts being' is a clumsy progressive calque for the change of state.

highlights.text: starts being abnormally aggressive

rows.jp: 「さっきの話と、どう関係があるんです？」
rows.en: “What does that have to do with what we were discussing?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "How is this related to what we were discussing earlier?"

rows.jp: 「キミは俺に正義を説いた」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You preached justice to me."

rows.jp: 「……道理をわきまえた相手として、俺を見ている」
rows.en: “...You see me as someone capable of listening to reason.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...you see me as someone who can tell right from wrong, who is reasonable."

rows.jp: 小ぶりの眉根が寄った。

ghs.en: The tiny gap between her eyebrows grew tighter.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that her small brows draw together. The English makes the gap between them the body part that tightens.

highlights.text: The tiny gap between her eyebrows grew tighter.

rows.jp: 「そういう意味では……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "But I did not mean..."
ghs.assessment: そういう意味では begins a hesitant concession, 'In that sense...' The English instead explicitly denies that she meant it.

highlights.text: But I did not mean...

rows.jp: 「そういう意味でしょ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You meant exactly that."

rows.jp: 「俺の行動をどうかと思う。そう指摘して弾劾する。直してもらわなければならないと思う」
rows.en: “You have doubts about my behavior. You point that out, you condemn me, and you believe I need to change.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You have a problem with my conduct. You point it out and denounce it. It is absolutely unthinkable for you not to come and fix me."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says she believes he must correct his conduct. The English makes Kiri personally come fix him and frames failure to do so as unthinkable.

highlights.text: It is absolutely unthinkable for you not to come and fix me.

rows.jp: 「群青でふりかざす考え方じゃないなぁ」
rows.en: “That’s not exactly a way of thinking people go around brandishing at Gunjo.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That ain't a way of thinking you can bandy around at Gunjou ya know."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says this is not a principle one should brandish at Gunjō. 'Bandy around' changes aggressive moral wielding into casual circulation, 'Gunjou' is non-Hepburn, and the eye dialect is unsupported.

highlights.text: Taichi: "That ain't a way of thinking you can bandy around at Gunjou ya know."

rows.jp: 「キミがただの鈍い子なのか、それとも逆に、鋭く俺の性根を見抜いているのかはわからない」
rows.en: “I don’t know whether you’re simply oblivious or whether you’ve seen straight through me to what I really am.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Whether you're just dumb, or conversely, you very sharply saw through my character I can't tell."
ghs.assessment: 鈍い means obtuse or insensitive here, not simply unintelligent. The English shifts the alternative insight into past tense and fails to close the embedded whether construction before the main clause.

highlights.text: Whether you're just dumb, or conversely, you very sharply saw through my character I can't tell.

rows.jp: 「けど……久しぶりに、新しい出会いの中で人間扱いされた気がした」
rows.en: “But... for the first time in a long while, a new acquaintance treated me like a human being.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But... it felt like a long time since I've been treated like a human by someone I just met."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says it felt like he had been treated as human for the first time in a long while. The English instead makes the elapsed time itself the feeling and mixes past and present perfect.

highlights.text: it felt like a long time since I've been treated

rows.jp: ぽかん、と口を開く。

ghs.en: She opens her mouth, agape.

rows.jp: 気を抜くと、なるほど歳相応に可愛らしい。
rows.en: With her guard down, she was, indeed, as cute as any girl her age.

ghs.en: When she loses focus a bit, she has the cuteness suitable for a girl her age.

rows.jp: 豊の目は節穴だな。

ghs.en: Yutaka's eyes are knotholes indeed.
ghs.assessment: 目は節穴 is an idiom meaning that Yutaka is a poor judge or effectively blind to her appeal. The English exposes the literal knotholes without conveying that function.

highlights.text: Yutaka's eyes are knotholes indeed.

rows.jp: 「……そーいう話をしているのではなく！」
rows.en: “...That is not what we were talking about!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...that isn't what we are talking about!"

rows.jp: 「みゆきは」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Miyuki, she..."

rows.jp: 激昂が凍りつく。

ghs.en: Her indignation freezes.

rows.jp: 「あれで結構、重いんだ」
rows.en: “She’s in fairly serious condition, despite appearances.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "She was quite serious... in that regard."
ghs.assessment: 重い here means that Miyuki's condition is fairly severe. 'Serious in that regard' is vague and can instead describe her attitude.

highlights.text: quite serious... in that regard

rows.jp: 「詳しくは知らないけど、本人が孤独を感じすぎると、発症するみたい」
rows.en: “I don’t know all the details, but apparently it manifests when she feels too alone.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I don't know the details, but, it seems that when she starts feeling excessively lonely her symptoms come out."
ghs.assessment: 発症する means that the condition manifests or she has an episode. Symptoms do not idiomatically 'come out' in English.

highlights.text: her symptoms come out

rows.jp: 「外界失認ってやつだ。世界の輪郭があいまいになる。一種のトリップだな。もっとも屋上から落ちやすいタイプ」
rows.en: “It’s called external-world agnosia. The contours of the world become indistinct—a kind of trip. Mind you, it’s the kind that makes you prone to falling from rooftops.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "She has External World Agnosia. The outline of the world becomes fuzzy and unclear. Kind of a drug trip. She's the type that'd fall from the rooftop easily."

rows.jp: 「知ってた？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Did you know?"
Kiri: "...no."

rows.jp: 「たぶんあの子は、移動になっちゃうと思うよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I think that she'll end up transferred, maybe."

rows.jp: 「え……移動というのは……？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Eh... what do you mean, transferred...?"

rows.jp: 「ちゃんとした病院施設に送られるってこと」
rows.en: “It means sending her to a proper hospital facility.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That she'll be sent to a proper hospitalization facility."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says she will be sent to a proper hospital facility. 'Hospitalization facility' is a nonstandard tautological compound.

highlights.text: proper hospitalization facility

rows.jp: 「それって……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "But that's..."

rows.jp: 霧は絶句したようだった。

ghs.en: Kiri appeared speechless.

rows.jp: 「ホラ、学校だとどうしても孤独な時間ってあるだろ？　周囲が全員健常者なら気づかってあげられるけどさ……みんな自分のことで精一杯だし」
rows.en: “Look, at school, time alone is unavoidable. If everyone around her were healthy, they could look out for her... but here, everyone has all they can do to manage themselves.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Come now, it's a school, aren't there hours where we're alone as a matter of course? If all around us there were healthy people they'd worry about it but... everyone's just doing what they can about themselves."

rows.jp: 「みゆきのもっとも嫌う、孤独な時ってのが、どこにでもある」
rows.en: “The loneliness Miyuki hates most is everywhere.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Those hours of solitude, what Miyuki hated most, they're everywhere."

rows.jp: たとえば放課後。誰もいない教室。
rows.en: After school, for example. An empty classroom.

ghs.en: For example, after school. A classroom with no one inside.

rows.jp: たとえば校庭。無人のトラック。
rows.en: Or the schoolyard. A track with no one on it.

ghs.en: For example, the courtyard. The sports track left depopulated.
ghs.assessment: 無人 means simply empty or unoccupied. 'Depopulated' implies an established population was removed.

highlights.text: depopulated

rows.jp: たとえば教室。人がいても人同士の接続がない、断絶空間。
rows.en: Or a classroom full of people but empty of connection—a space of absolute separation.

ghs.en: For example, the classroom. There are people, but no one to have a connection or a fellowship with; it is a space of disintegration.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes a room where people are present but disconnected from one another, a space of severance. The English instead says there is no available person to connect with and calls the space one of disintegration.

highlights.text: For example, the classroom. There are people, but no one to have a connection or a fellowship with; it is a space of disintegration.

rows.jp: 「どこにだって空白はあるのさ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wherever you go there are vacuums, you know."

rows.jp: 「彼女が放送部に入ってるのは、ウチが自意識を保持している連中の集団だからだ」
rows.en: “She joined the broadcasting club because we’re a group of people who still retain a sense of self.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "She had joined the Broadcast Club because this in-group was an assembly of people maintaining a sense of self."
ghs.assessment: ウチ means their club, not a sociological in-group. The English also shifts the continuing reason for her membership into past tense and uses an abstract 'assembly.'

highlights.text: this in-group was an assembly

rows.jp: 「そういう意図のもとで放送部は成立してる」
rows.en: “That is the intent on which the broadcasting club was founded.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The Broadcast Club had been established with that intention as foundation."
ghs.assessment: The club exists on the basis of that intention. The English uses past perfect for an ongoing institution and omits the determiner before 'foundation.'

highlights.text: had been established with that intention as foundation

rows.jp: 「他に部活なんていくつもないからね」
rows.en: “It’s not as though there are many other clubs.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "'Cause there's not much activity in the club besides that, you know."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says there are not many other clubs. The English instead says this club contains little activity beyond the stated purpose.

highlights.text: there's not much activity in the club besides that

rows.jp: 肩をすくめた。

ghs.en: I shrugged my shoulders.

rows.jp: 「友達を作るのは大変だ。でも作らずにはいられない。どうしてかわかる？」
rows.en: “Making friends is hard. But we can’t help trying. Do you know why?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Making friends is a hassle. But going without making some is unacceptable. Do you know why?"
ghs.assessment: 大変 means difficult, not merely bothersome. 作らずにはいられない says people cannot help making friends, whereas the English turns that compulsion into a normative prohibition.

highlights.text: a hassle
going without making some is unacceptable

ghs.en: Kiri: "...no."

rows.jp: 「必要だからだ。心を育てるためには」
rows.en: “Because we need them. To let our hearts grow.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because they're necessary. Necessary for the rearing of a heart."
ghs.assessment: 心を育てる means nurturing emotional or mental development. 'Rearing' ordinarily applies to children or animals and treats a heart as an independent creature.

highlights.text: the rearing of a heart

rows.jp: 「豊とは友人になれた。これはいいことだよな」
rows.en: “I managed to become friends with Yutaka. That’s a good thing, right?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yutaka became a friend. That's a good thing."

rows.jp: 「みゆきともなりたいと思った。けど、ちょっとやり方がまずかったかもしれない」
rows.en: “I wanted to become friends with Miyuki, too. But maybe I went about it badly.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I thought I would also have Miyuki become one. But the way I used wasn't quite the right one, maybe."
ghs.assessment: Taichi wanted to become friends with Miyuki. The English instead makes him cause Miyuki to become an unspecified object called 'one.'

highlights.text: I thought I would also have Miyuki become one.

rows.jp: 「けど俺は、こんなことくらいしか知らなくてなぁ」
rows.en: “But this is about the only way I know.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But me, outside of that I don't really know what to do!"

rows.jp: 苦笑する。

ghs.en: A wry smile.

rows.jp: 「やっぱ俺もクレバーだもんでさ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm really so clevah aren't I."

rows.jp: 「……じゃあ……セクハラしてたのって……わざとですか？」
rows.en: “...Then... were you sexually harassing her... deliberately?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...so... that sexual harassment... it is on purpose?"
ghs.assessment: Kiri asks whether the past harassment was deliberate. The English changes it to present tense and uses declarative question order.

highlights.text: it is on purpose?

rows.jp: 「下心もあるよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "There's an ulterior motive too."

rows.jp: 正直に答える。

ghs.en: I answer honestly.

rows.jp: 「ぐっ」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Ngh..."

rows.jp: 「俺って理性が異常に脆くてさ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Me, my rationality's unusually fragile."

rows.jp: 「けど、意識的な部分もある」

ghs.en: Taichi: "But there's a part of it that is deliberate."

rows.jp: 「あの地味子ちゃんの、思い出の一つにでもなればなぁと」
rows.en: “I thought I might at least become one of that plain little girl’s memories.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I wanted to make that plain girl into one of my memories, that's it."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says he hoped the act might become one of the plain girl's memories. The English reverses possessor and object, making the girl into one of Taichi's memories.

highlights.text: make that plain girl into one of my memories

rows.jp: コゼーからポットを取り出す。
rows.en: I took the pot from its tea cozy.

ghs.en: I took the pot from the tea cozy.

rows.jp: まだ熱い。いいコゼーを使っていた。
rows.en: It was still hot. They had a good tea cozy.

ghs.en: Still hot. They were using a good cozy.

rows.jp: 紅茶をカップに注いで、そのまま飲む。
rows.en: I poured tea into the cup and drank it straight.

ghs.en: I pour black tea into the cup and drink it straight.

rows.jp: 「みんな繋がりが欲しい」

ghs.en: Taichi: "We all desire connection."

rows.jp: 「俺たちだけじゃない。誰だって欲しい」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's not just the likes of us. Everybody does."

rows.jp: 「携帯、ネット、手紙、友達」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Telephone, the 'net, letters, friendship."
ghs.assessment: 携帯 here means mobile phones or cellphones, not telephones in general.

highlights.text: Telephone

rows.jp: 「みんな繋がりじゃないか」

ghs.en: Taichi: "All connections, aren't they?"

rows.jp: 「そこに誰かいると期待して、言葉や情報や電波を発信するんじゃないか」
rows.en: “We send out words and information and signals because we hope someone is there, don’t we?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "we dispatch language and information and radio waves because of that expectation that someone'll be there, isn't it?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks whether people transmit those things expecting someone to be there. The English begins the sentence lowercase, uses 'dispatch' for communication, and attaches a singular tag to a plural subject.

highlights.text: we dispatch language and information and radio waves because of that expectation that someone'll be there, isn't it?

rows.jp: 「俺は自分が触れる相手が、がらんどうだなんて思いたくない」
rows.en: “I don’t want to believe the person I can touch is hollow inside.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Me, I don't want to think that the partner I'm touching is just a human-shaped hollow."

rows.jp: 「だからセクハラする。し続ける」
rows.en: “So I sexually harass people. And I will keep doing it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Therefore I perform sexual harassment. And I will continue to."

rows.jp: 「……キミがどんなに止めてもやーめない」
rows.en: “...No matter how hard you try to stop me, I won’t.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...you can stop me however much you like but I'll neeever stop forever!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese emphatically says he will not stop. The English redundantly adds 'forever' to 'never' and stretches the wrong lexical material.

highlights.text: neeever stop forever

rows.jp: 飲み干す。

ghs.en: I drink the cup empty.

rows.jp: 「止めたかったら、止めれば。キックでも腕ひしぎでもシックスナインでも」
rows.en: “If you want to stop me, then stop me. Kick me, put me in an arm lock, sixty-nine me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Try to stop me if you want me to stop. With kicks or face grabs or sixty-nine."
ghs.assessment: 腕ひしぎ is an arm lock, not a grab to the face.

highlights.text: face grabs

rows.jp: 「……シックスナイン？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...sixty-nine?"

rows.jp: 「またそうすることで、キミと俺との繋がりができれば、いいなと思うよ。キミは迷惑かも知れないけど」
rows.en: “And if that creates another connection between you and me, I’d like that. Even if it’s a nuisance to you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because if you and me manage to be connected by doing that again, I think it'd be a good thing. It might be annoying to you, however."

rows.jp: うつむいて。

ghs.en: Downcast,

rows.jp: 少女は思索にふけった。

ghs.en: the girl lost herself in meditation.

rows.jp: 俺が突き落とした、思考の迷宮に。
rows.en: Into the labyrinth of thought I had shoved her.

ghs.en: Into the labyrinth of thoughts that I pushed her down into.

rows.jp: 自分の吐いた言葉を反芻する。
rows.en: I turned my own words over again.

ghs.en: Thinking over and over the words I lied out,
ghs.assessment: 吐いた言葉 means the words he uttered or spat out. 'Lied out' both invents deliberate falsehood at this point and is not an English phrasal verb.

highlights.text: words I lied out

rows.jp: まるで自分が『不健全ながらも頑張ってる』みたいな。
rows.en: As if I were telling a story in which I was unhealthy but trying my best.

ghs.en: it's just like there's something there that says, "he's hardworking, unwholesomeness notwithstanding".
ghs.assessment: Taichi reflects that he has made himself sound like someone trying hard despite being unhealthy. The English invents an external 'something' that says this and shifts self-reference into third person.

highlights.text: it's just like there's something there that says, "he's hardworking, unwholesomeness notwithstanding"

rows.jp: そんな欺瞞(ぎまん)さえ呑み込んで、奥底に隠そうとする意識があった。
rows.en: Some part of me was even swallowing that deception and trying to bury it deep.

ghs.en: There was intent to swallow that deceit, hiding it in the very bottom of the heart.

rows.jp: 「納得は、できません」

ghs.en: Kiri: "I... cannot agree to that."

rows.jp: やがて霧は決然と言った。
rows.en: At last, Kiri spoke with resolve.

ghs.en: So said Kiri not long afterwards, resolute.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri eventually speaks with resolve. The English uses an archaic inversion and leaves the adjective 'resolute' dangling after the clause.

highlights.text: So said Kiri not long afterwards, resolute.

rows.jp: 「今は、それくらいしか……」
rows.en: “For now, that is all I can say...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Right now, I have nothing more than that..."

rows.jp: 「そう」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well."
ghs.assessment: そう acknowledges her answer, like 'I see.' 'Well' signals hesitation or transition instead.

highlights.text: Well.

rows.jp: それで良かった。

ghs.en: Then that's good.

rows.jp: 簡単に騙されてはダメだ。
rows.en: She could not let herself be deceived so easily.

ghs.en: Being easily deceived is unacceptable.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese directly says one must not be easily deceived. The English turns this into an impersonal judgment of acceptability.

highlights.text: Being easily deceived is unacceptable.

rows.jp: 世界はあまりにも汚れているのだから。
rows.en: The world was far too filthy for that.

ghs.en: The world is far too dirty for that.

rows.jp: 「それはそれとして、改めまして佐倉霧です」
rows.en: “That aside, let me introduce myself again. I’m Kiri Sakura.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Be that as it may, once again, I am Sakura Kiri."

rows.jp: 礼儀正しく頭を下げた。

ghs.en: She bows her head with thorough politeness.
Taichi: "Eh?"

rows.jp: 「佐倉……霧です」

ghs.en: Kiri: "I am Sakura... Kiri."

rows.jp: 「あ、うん。黒須太一です」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, yes. I am Kurosu Taichi."

rows.jp: 結局、ぎこちない対面式だった。
rows.en: In the end, our introduction was still awkward.

ghs.en: In the end, it was an awkward embarrassed face-to-face meeting.

rows.jp: 「さて、じゃ俺はそろそろ帰るけど……豊も寝てるし……」
rows.en: “Well, I should be heading home... Yutaka’s asleep, too...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "So then, it's about time I get on the way home, but... Yutaka's still sleeping..."

rows.jp: 立ち上がる。

ghs.en: I rise.

rows.jp: 「すいません。よく、寝るんです」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Apologies. He is a... frequent sleeper."
ghs.assessment: よく寝る means that he sleeps a lot. The English classifies him as a type of sleeper and inserts an unsupported hesitation.

highlights.text: a... frequent sleeper

rows.jp: 「そうそう、もし潤いが欲しかったら、放送部に来るといい」
rows.en: “Oh, one more thing. If you want a little more life around you, come by the broadcasting club.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Right, right, so if want a little enrichment to your heart, do come to the Broadcast Club."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese invites Kiri to the club if she wants emotional enrichment. The English omits the subject 'you' and uses a cumbersome prepositional phrase.

highlights.text: so if want a little enrichment to your heart

ghs.en: Kiri: "...yes."

rows.jp: 「けど来たら、いじるぞ。覚悟の上、それなりに対策してから来るように」
